title: Softly Fades the Twilight Ray
description: Softly Fades the Twilight Ray in Tonic Solfa to INNOCENTS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Samuel Francis Smith wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 79 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Sabbath Evening”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to INNOCENTS; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Soft-ly fades the twi-light ray Of the ho-ly Sab-bath day; Gen-tly as life's set-ting sun; When the Christ-ian's course is run.

lines: When the Christian's course is run.
O'er the earth, as daylight fades;
All things tell of calm repose
Peace is on the world abroad;
When the spirit rests from sin.

licence: Public domain: Samuel Francis Smith died in 1895.
credits: Words by Samuel Francis Smith (1808–1895), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to INNOCENTS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
